summary: 35 units reviewed against the printed Devanagari. 1 error (u41: printed bhajaṃti silently restored as bhajante with no flag; `w` patched to bhajanti). Minor: Hindi additions (u40 bare मल, u53 जैसे/चिह्न, u55/u64 ही, u65 उसको, u39 added हो and no doubt mark), u52 dangling 'or;', u54 -rātrāt labelled feminine, u56 emendation ārdreṣu unmarked in translations, u58 'Loose' unhedged, spacing typos u49/u58 only in notes (flags added), and continuation wording in notes hedged with 'appears to'. Checked and found sound: no ai/au hiatus problem in any flagged sandhi (u42, u51, u54, u56, u60, u67 Devanagari read); u67 vidahyate conjecture good; identifications kumuda/utpala (probable), padminī, candana, vaṅkṣaṇa, pretādhipa (Yama, probable) are correct and suitably hedged; no wrong identifications. Needs a human decision: u39 (anyo'nyo'pi, gata), u53 (sīmantāvartaka), u60 (māsān vs māsāt, which form goes in words), u63/u64 grammar, u52 sasneham/vā māsāntam, and whether letter-level corrections need the conjectural mark. No regrouping suggested (45-46, 47-48, 49-50, 51-52, 55-56, 57-58, 61-62, 63-64, 65-66, 67-68, 69-70 read as drafted; 53-54 one sentence).
glossary_suggestions: bhajanti (parasmaipada) vs printed tyajaṃte (ātmanepada): keep printed forms in `w`, never silently normalise voice.
-rātra dvigu ablatives (ṣaḍ-rātrāt, tri-rātrāt): gram 'dvigu, abl. sg.', not feminine.
Hindi mala = 'मल यानी अपशिष्ट' also in lists of body parts (ch09 u40).
Missing-space tokens (yasyaromakūpāśca, tṛṣṇāca) get a text_flag as well as a note.
bhinna purīṣa: 'broken stool (probably loose)', Hindi 'भिन्न यानी टूटा हुआ, सम्भवतः ढीला, मल'.
pretādhipa = lord of the departed, probably Yama (hedged in both languages); kumuda = probably white water lily, utpala = probably blue water lily (Nymphaea nouchali).
Decide book-wide: do letter-level typo corrections adopted in `words` (straṃsaḥ→sraṃsaḥ, cūrṇa→cūrṇam) need the conjectural mark in translations, or only word-replacing ones (ārdveṣu→ārdreṣu)?
